subject: PO Serialization, Spend Ceiling Override & Line-Item Patchwork
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@lumos-tech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Initial vendor paperwork & provisional PO request

Hi Amy,

Thanks for starting the onboarding process with Redwood. To get a provisional PO in place while we finish vendor setup, we need: 
- Completed vendor onboarding form (attached)
- W9 / tax docs (if US)
- Primary billing contact and invoice email
- Expected spend profile (monthly cadence and any seasonality) and whether you need a single PO or split POs for test vs prod.

Our standard provisional spend cap is $50,000. If you anticipate higher usage in Q1 we can discuss an override; please indicate the target cap and a short justification.

I'll route the provisional PO as a serialized PO number (one master PO with sub-line items) unless you request separate PO numbers per environment. Attachments: lumos_onboarding_form.xlsx (Excel)

Thanks — kim

--
Kimberly Park
Sr. Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
[attachment: lumos_onboarding_form.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Amy Chen <amy@lumos-tech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumos Procurement <procure@lumos-tech.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial vendor paperwork & provisional PO request

Hi Kimberly,

Appreciate the checklist. Attaching our W9 and a quick summary of expected spend: 30k in Dec (ramp), then ~20k/mo thereafter. We're flexible on single vs split POs but prefer separate lines for sandbox/test (cap $5k) and production.

Questions from our side:
1) Can Redwood issue a single master PO with two line-item caps (test/prod) or do you need two distinct PO numbers?
2) If we request a one-time higher provisional cap ($75k) for onboarding and initial migration, what's the approval path and SLA?

Attached: lumos_w9.pdf (PDF)

Thanks — Amy
Amy Chen
Vendor Ops | Lumos Tech
amy@lumos-tech.com
[attachment: lumos_w9.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@lumos-tech.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial vendor paperwork & provisional PO request

Hi Amy / Kim,

Quick procurement note: we can issue a serialized PO (PO 4321) that contains two capped line items — one for SANDBOX (line 1, cap $5,000) and one for PROD (line 2). Standard provisional cap default is $50,000. For a one-time ramp to $75,000 we need a short business justification and manager approval (I can route to Finance; expect 24-48 hr turnaround during business days).

Action items:
- Amy: confirm you accept serialized PO with line-level caps (yes/no)
- Amy: confirm invoice email and legal remit-to address (for our AP)
- Kim: can you kick off the PO template? I've attached the provisional_po_template.csv with the two-line layout I propose.

Also flag: when I mapped Lumos' SKUs into our ledger I noticed two mismatches (Lumos item ID 17-AX vs internal SKU 17-A). That will require a line-item correction on issuance if Lumos expects to bill under 17-AX.

Attached: provisional_po_template.csv (CSV)

Cheers,
Ben
Procurement Operations | Redwood Inference
[attachment: provisional_po_template.csv (CSV)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial vendor paperwork & provisional PO request (line-item mapping)

Ben / Kim — looping in because I want to avoid a billing mismatch on day one. Observations: 
- Lumos' invoice will reference 17-AX and 22-BZ. Our ledger expects 17-A and 22-BZ-1.
- Proposal: issue PO 4321 with the vendor-facing line description matching Lumos (17-AX) and include an internal note mapping to our SKU (17-A). That way AP can match invoices to the vendor lines and we keep internal accounting consistent.

If we issue a separate PO for test/prod, we'll need to replicate mapping on both POs. That adds friction for the vendor, so I prefer the serialized PO + vendor-visible line labels.

Please confirm and I'll add the internal ledger mapping in the procurement ticket (PR-7892).

—Priyom
Senior Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@lumos-tech.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-23T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Final: PO 4321 issued (serialized) + spend cap amendment approved

Amy — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and links: 

- We've issued Provisional PO 4321 as a serialized PO with two vendor-facing lines: 
  * Line 1 (SANDBOX) — cap $5,000
  * Line 2 (PROD) — cap $70,000 (one-time ramp to $75k was approved by Finance; we set the working cap to $70k and will release up to $75k pending final spend review)
- Internal mapping: procurement will attach ledger crosswalks so invoices referencing 17-AX will match internal SKU 17-A (per Priyom).
- Attachments: final_PO_4321.pdf (formal PO), lumos_onboarding_form_filled.xlsx (vendor-submitted), lumos_w9.pdf (vendor tax doc).
- DocuSign for vendor signature: https://docusign.com/XYZ-PO-4321
- Procurement ticket: PR-7892 (I've added notes and flagged the line-item mapping).

Amy — please countersign DocuSign and send the billing email (accounts@lumos-tech.com) if different from the one on file. Ben / Priyom — please push the internal ledger mapping into PR-7892 and confirm once AP has the final_PO_4321.pdf.

If anything unexpected comes up, I'll escalate to Finance.

Thanks everyone — happy holidays, and welcome aboard Lumos.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
[attachment: final_PO_4321.pdf (PDF)]
